Abu Waa'il (RAH) narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once heard a person saying, "Where are the people who have no concern for this world and look forward to the Aakhirah?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said to him, "They are the people of Jaabiya[^2]. They were five hundred Muslim men who pledged that they would be martyred in battle and not return home. (Therefore, according to their custom,) They shaved off their hair, fought the enemy and were all martyred besides one who lived to tell the tale." [^3]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once heard a person saying, "Where are the people who have no concern for this world and look forward to the Aakhirah?" Taking the person to the graves of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said to him, "Were you asking about these personalities?" [^4]

Abu Araaka (RAH) narrates that he once performed the Fajr salaah behind Hadhrat Ali (RA). After the salaah, Hadhrat Ali (RA) turned to his right and appeared to be extremely troubled. Eventually, when the sun rose the length of a spear's length above the Masjid wall, he performed two Rakaahs of salaah. Thereafter, he turned his hands over and said, "By Allaah! I have seen the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ and do not see the likes of them anywhere today. In the mornings, their faces were pale, their hair dishevelled, their bodies covered in dust and between their eyes were the marks of prostration which resembled the marks on the knees of goats. Their nights were spent prostrating (in Sajdah) and standing before Allaah (in salaah). They recited the Book of Allaah (the Qur'aan) and would attain comfort by standing in salaah and making Sajdah. When the mornings arrived and they engaged in Dhikr, their bodies would move as the trees do when the gentle wind blows through them. Their eyes would flow with tears until their clothing got wet as if they (were remorseful because they) had spent their nights in negligence." Thereafter, Hadhrat Ali (RA) stood up and was never again seen laughing quietly until he was martyred by the wicked enemy of Allaah, Ibn Muljim. [^5]

Hadhrat Diraar bin Damirah Kinaani (RAH) once came to Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA), who asked him to describe Hadhrat Ali (RA). Hadhrat Diraar bin Damirah Kinaani (RAH) said, "Would you excuse me?" Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) replied, "You cannot be excused." Hadhrat Diraar bin Damirah Kinaani (RAH) continued, "If I have to say something, then I swear by Allaah that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was a man of high objectives (with immense honour).
